evidence.gaps:
I found no press-reported, filing-based or rating-agency figure for Jump Trading GROUP net trading revenue, revenue, profit or EBITDA for any year 2015-2026, and no 2026 YTD figure of any kind. Bloomberg, FT, WSJ, Reuters and Business Insider have apparently never published a sourced Jump group revenue number in this period. The last solid group-ish figures are Bloomberg's (2014), drawn from SEC filings: 2008 profit $316M, and 2010 operating revenue $512M with net income $268M.

The shared web-search budget ran out after about 12 queries, early in the task. The planned year-by-year and outlet-by-outlet sweep, especially for 2015-2019, was NOT completed. I worked from direct fetches of known documents instead.

Highest-value follow-ups:
(1) S&P and Moody's reports on Jump Financial LLC, the group's ultimate parent. The ratings are S&P BB- (outlook revised from negative to stable in 2024) and Moody's Ba1 CFR / Ba2 TLB. The full reports usually give revenue, EBITDA and capital, but they are paywalled (the S&P page returned 403).
(2) Leveraged-loan coverage (Bloomberg, LCD, 9fin, Octus, IFR) of the 2021 $300M TLB due 2028, the Mar 2022 $200M add-on and the Feb 2025 $750M issuance. Lender materials are often quoted with revenue and EBITDA.
(3) Dutch KvK accounts of Jump Trading Europe B.V. (EU trading since 2019); Singapore ACRA accounts of Jump Trading Pacific Pte; Indian MCA filings for Jump Trading Financial India.
(4) Pre-2014 Jump Trading LLC X-17A-5 income statements (the source of the Bloomberg 2010 figures).
(5) Bloomberg's 2026-09-17 piece/video on high-speed traders' India profits, and SEBI materials, for any Jump India figure.

Not retrieved: the UK FY2024 accounts themselves (2024 values come from FY2025 comparatives), the UK FY2018 accounts (2018 values come from FY2019 comparatives), and pre-2014 UK accounts. Firm-wide headcount by year is not established here: only UK-entity series plus unsourced secondary claims of 1,500-2,000+.
evidence.red_flags:
1) Entity confusion is the reverse of the orchestrator's hint. Jump Financial, LLC is the ULTIMATE PARENT of Jump Trading Holdings LLC (Jump Trading LLC X-17A-5 FY2024, Note 1), so Moody's and S&P ratings and term loans of 'Jump Financial' are the Jump Trading group's. Tai Mo Shan Ltd sits under Jump Crypto Holdings LLC.

2) Terra profit figures are inconsistent and circular. The $1.28B comes from the SEC's Feb 2023 complaint against Terraform (Jump unnamed). Class-action plaintiffs (Patterson, Kim) then copied it, followed by Medium and AI-written sites (e.g. 'a 2,780% return', '$123M = 9.6% of profits'). The SEC's own settled order against Tai Mo Shan (Dec 2024) quantified only about $73.45M of profit, from the amended July 2021 agreement. The WSJ (Dec 2025) says 'about $1 billion'. Whatever the true number, it is a crypto token gain realised mostly in 2021, not annual net trading revenue. The $123M settlement is a cost.

3) Company-data aggregator revenue estimates are mutually inconsistent and not credible: ZoomInfo $952M, Owler $0.5-1B, Bitscale $546M, Growjo $340M, Levels.fyi $100-250M, LeadIQ $1-10B. All are undated model outputs.

4) The fi-desk article (May 2025) mis-scales net capital as 'US$220,883'. The filing is in thousands, so the actual figure is $220.9M.

5) UK accounts traps:
- FY2015 revenue was restated, from 'Turnover' $119.0M to 'Revenue, net' $159.1M, with expenses grossed up and profit unchanged.
- 2015 staff costs were later reclassified.
- From mid-2019 the UK entity is a research/back-office SERVICE company paid under transfer pricing. Its 2020+ 'revenue' is NOT trading revenue and must not be added to group PnL.
- European trading moved to Jump Trading Europe B.V. (Netherlands) in 2019.

6) Headcount claims conflict: Wikipedia '2000+' (uncited), the newsletters ~1,600 and ~1,500, Grokipedia 1,400-1,800. None trace to a primary source.

7) insights4vc is internally contradictory: FTX loss of '$27M' vs its own cited CoinDesk headline of ~$300M; 2021 profit '$500M-1B' vs a Terra gain of '$1.28B'.

8) The youngandcalculated (Quant Enthusiasts) newsletter misattributes Terraform's $4.4-4.5B SEC liability ambiguously in a Jump context.

9) A Medium post presents '$123M regulatory cost' as a share of the $1.28B. This is derivative arithmetic on an unproven figure.
evidence.summary:
Jump is the most opaque firm in the set. No reliable press figure exists for group net trading revenue in any year 2015-2026, and there is nothing for 2026 YTD (cutoff: no data as of 2026-10-08). Search budget ran out early, so a full outlet-by-outlet press sweep was not completed.

**Verified hard anchors:**
- Bloomberg (2014), from SEC filings: US entity 2010 operating revenue $512M and net income $268M; 2008 profit $316M; about 350 staff in 2014.
- A newly assembled primary series from the UK subsidiary's audited accounts (Jump Trading International Ltd, Companies House 05976015, read by OCR):
  - 2015-2018 net trading revenue (Europe slice): $159M, $158M, $154M, $207M.
  - Average UK headcount: 49 (2015), 68, 94, 114, 138, 154, 183, 246, 275, 288, 319 (2025).
  - UK staff cost per head: about $0.6-0.7M in 2016-2019, $1.15M (2020), $1.20M (2021), $1.07M (2022), $0.95M (2023), $0.84M (2024), $1.29M (2025).
  - 2025 UK staff costs were $410M (+71%), with a 'higher year-end accrued bonus pool'.
  - This comp-per-head pattern is the best available proxy for group results: strong 2020-21, softer 2022-24, and 2025 probably a record year.
- Crypto items:
  - Terra/LUNA: the SEC alleged about $1.28B, the WSJ says about $1B, and the SEC-adjudicated Tai Mo Shan profit is only $73.45M.
  - 2022 losses: Wormhole replenishment about $320M; FTX about $300M.
  - 2024 SEC settlement: $123M.
- Debt and ratings for Jump Financial LLC (the group's parent): $300M TLB in 2021, a $200M add-on in Mar 2022, $750M of debt in Feb 2025. S&P BB- (stable since 2024); Moody's Ba1 CFR.

**Indicative group NTR (my judgement only, not reported figures).** Method: UK comp per head times a plausible firm-wide headcount of about 700-1,700, divided by a 25-50% comp ratio, cross-checked against peers (2025: HRT about $11M per head, IMC about $1.6M per head).

evidence.gaps: No disclosed firm-wide PnL, net trading revenue, profit or EBITDA for Jump Trading Group for any year 2015-2026. Jump has no public debt, no rating-agency coverage and no leveraged-finance deals that I found, so there are no Moody's/S&P/Fitch/KBRA or 9fin/Octus figures. Public X-17A-5 filings for Jump Trading LLC hold only a balance sheet, with no income statement or headcount; the FOCUS Part II is confidential. No firm-wide headcount time series is disclosed. I built a primary proxy from US 401(k) Form 5500 active participants plus the UK group's filed headcount, but rest-of-world staff (Singapore, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Mumbai/GIFT City, Amsterdam) have no free filings: ACRA, ASIC, KvK and Indian MCA are paywalled or need a login. 2026 YTD: no PnL data at all. The latest primary cutoffs are the UK FY2025 accounts (filed 2026-09-29), Form 5500 plan year 2025 (filed 2026-08-28) and X-17A-5 FY2025 (filed 2026-03-02). The only 2026 headcount indicator is the homepage claim of '2000+ employees', fetched 2026-10-08. Not checked: Terraform trial testimony, the later SEC amended complaint that holds the $1.28bn figure, the Taewoo Kim class-action complaint, the CFTC probe outcome and FTX-claim documents. The shared web-search budget (200 calls per turn) ran out after 6 searches, so no further press searches (Bloomberg, FT, WSJ, The Information, Forbes billionaire profiles) were possible. Primary documents were fetched directly instead. Year-specific firm-wide revenue reports in top-tier press remain unverified and unsearched.
evidence.red_flags: 1) The UK subsidiary's revenue is transfer-pricing income for a service company from 2019, when the UK entity was de-authorised by the FCA and has had 'no proprietary trading book' since. Before 2019 it mixed its own prop-trading profits with transfer-pricing allocations. It must not be treated as Jump trading revenue. 2) FY2015 was restated: originally reported turnover was $119.0m, the FY2016 comparative shows $159.1m (recharge income grossed up). The 2015 average headcount is 49 in the original filing and 47 in the FY2016 comparative. 3) eFinancialCareers (Oct-2024) reported 2023 UK headcount as 271 and 'profits' as $66.6m. The filing shows an average of 275, a year-end count of 281, operating profit of $66.6m and net profit of $51.7m: the article mixes metrics and uses the prior year's headcount. 4) The $1.28bn Terra gain is an allegation that originated in SEC v. Terraform filings and was repeated by Fortune, a class action, Wikipedia and blogs (circular sourcing). The SEC's final Dec-2024 order against Tai Mo Shan quantified only $73.45m profit, for the amended-agreement LUNA. The $1.28bn spans 2021-22 and is token-sale gains, not calendar trading revenue. The $123m settlement is a 2024 cost. 5) Aggregator revenue figures disagree wildly and should all be rejected: PrivCo 2021 revenue $120M / net income $12M; ZoomInfo $952M; Owler $500M-1B; Bitscale $546M. 6) Headcount claims are inconsistent: homepage and Wikipedia say 2000+ (Wikipedia's citation does not support it), BuiltIn 1,488, Substack ~1,500, Bitscale 924. Primary US (1,125) plus UK (336) totals 1,461 at YE2025. 7) The Form 5500 welfare-plan participant counts are erratic: 1,575 at May 2023, then 948, against roughly 1,000 in the 401(k). They are not usable. 8) The insights4vc Substack is internally inconsistent on FTX exposure ($27M vs a $264M claim vs ~$300M) and on Terra (gain vs 'high-nine-figure losses').
evidence.summary:
Primary-document lens. No filing discloses firm-wide PnL for Jump. I did find two strong primary time series.

(a) UK Companies House accounts for Jump Trading International Ltd, FY2015-FY2025. I read every year from the filed PDFs or iXBRL. They give UK revenue, profit, average and year-end headcount, and wages.
- UK wages per average head ($k): 2015 ~1,340; 2016 1,016; 2017 483; 2018 532; 2019 567; 2020 1,008; 2021 1,027 (directors' pay spiked to $33.5m); 2022 907; 2023 812; 2024 687; 2025 1,071.
- This index tracks Jump's bonus cycle: weak 2017-19, boom 2020-21, decline 2022-24, strong 2025 (UK wages +73% to $341.7m; FY2025 accounts filed 2026-09-29).
- The UK mix was trader-heavy before 2018, so 2015-16 are not comparable.

(b) DOL Form 5500 401(k) active participants for Jump Operations LLC, the US employer, at each year-end: 2015 535; 2016 578; 2017 565; 2018 535; 2019 588; 2020 637; 2021 797; 2022 995; 2023 1,010; 2024 1,006; 2025 1,125.
- US plus UK at year-end: 2015 ~582, 2016 646, 2017 659, 2018 659, 2019 727, 2020 802, 2021 1,002, 2022 1,266, 2023 1,291, 2024 1,306, 2025 1,461.
- Adding an assumed 15-30% for rest-of-world offices gives my firm-wide average headcount estimate: 2015 ~620 (560-700), 2016 ~750 (690-830), 2017 ~800 (730-880), 2018 ~800 (730-880), 2019 ~840 (770-930), 2020 ~920 (840-1,020), 2021 ~1,080 (990-1,200), 2022 ~1,370 (1,250-1,520), 2023 ~1,530 (1,400-1,700), 2024 ~1,560 (1,420-1,740), 2025 ~1,730 (1,560-1,950).
- Year-end 2025 is ~1,800 (1,650-2,100). For 2026 YTD the homepage claims '2000+' (fetched 2026-10-08).

My derived net-trading-revenue estimates. These are not sourced figures. Method: firm wage pool ≈ global heads × UK wages per head, divided by an assumed comp ratio of 25-45% (higher in weak years), then sanity-checked against peers. In USD bn:
- 2015 ~1.3 (0.7-2.5)
- 2016 ~1.1 (0.6-2.2)
- 2017 ~0.9 (0.5-1.7)
- 2018 ~1.1 (0.6-1.9)
- 2019 ~1.2 (0.7-2.0)
- 2020 ~2.7 (1.7-4.2)
- 2021 ~3.6 (2.2-5.5), including crypto and Terra; the $1.28bn alleged gain spans 2021-22
- 2022 ~2.8 (1.5-4.5), net of crypto losses (Wormhole ~$321m, FTX)
- 2023 ~2.5 (1.5-4.0)
- 2024 ~2.4 (1.5-3.8)
- 2025 ~5.0 (3.0-7.5)
- 2026 YTD: no data.

Implied PnL per head is roughly $1.1-1.5m in 2017-19, ~$3m in 2020-21, ~$1.5-2m in 2022-24 and ~$3m in 2025. That is well below HRT and Jane Street per head, consistent with Jump's lower UK pay per head.

Other primary items:
- SEC order 33-11349 (2024-12-20): Tai Mo Shan's profit was ~$73.45m on the amended-agreement LUNA; the total payment was $123.1m.
- Jump Trading LLC (the US broker-dealer) member's equity: $122.0m (2018), $128.5m (2019), ~$206.5m (2022), $321.9m (2025). It is a balance sheet only.
